mainTopic: Whether items excluded from אונאה (land and הקדש) can have a sale cancelled, and the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about paying the missing value of a redeemed sacred animal
overview: This amud first ends רבא's question about kernels planted before the עומר with תיקו: it stays unresolved. A new topic then opens. רבי אמי asks whether items that have no אונאה, like land and הקדש, can still have a sale cancelled (ביטול מקח), and he answers that they can. רבי יונה applies this ruling from רבי יוחנן to הקדש, and רבי ירמיה applies it to land. The גמרא explains the gap between these two versions using שמואל's rule that הקדש redeemed for a פרוטה is redeemed. Next comes a משנה about a blemished sacred animal. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue over whether paying its missing value is a Torah law or a rabbinic law. The גמרא tests both possible price gaps, and it resolves the problem by switching the names. It then explains the argument through שמואל in two ways. Finally, it offers another answer that keeps the original names and ties the argument to רב חסדא's reading of 'אין להם אונאה', which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: May the planted kernels be picked and eaten after the עומר?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether kernels in the ground that did not take root are like kernels sitting in a jug, which the עומר permits, or whether they count as part of the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law about picking these kernels and eating them? Are they like kernels thrown into a jug, so the עומר made them permitted? Or perhaps the owner made them part of the ground?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes stating רבא's question about kernels that were put in the ground: may a person pick them up and eat them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to see these kernels. If they are just being stored in the ground, like grain in a jug, then the עומר permitted them like any other grain. If the owner made them part of the land, they are treated like seeds that did not take root, and they stay forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: to pick up, to gather
a jug or jar
the barley offering that permits the new year's grain
he made them part of the ground

phrases.english: What is the law about picking and eating from them?
phrases.notes: "Them" means the wheat kernels put into the ground, which רבא was just discussing.

phrases.english: Are they like kernels thrown into a jug,
so the עומר made them permitted,
or perhaps he made them part of the ground?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's question from the previous section of the דף
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are kernels in the ground that did not take root treated as stored grain, which the עומר permits, or as part of the land, which stays forbidden?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends רבא's question with תיקו: it stays unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says it has no answer to רבא's question, so the question is left open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no source was found to decide between the two sides. The topic ends here, and the גמרא moves on to something new.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand: the question remains unanswered

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the question was foolish. It means both sides stay possible, and later authorities have to decide how to rule in practice.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question raised in step 1
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's question about the planted kernels is left unresolved.

steps.title: Can a sale be cancelled for items that have no אונאה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי asks whether items excluded from אונאה can still have the sale cancelled when the price is very far off.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said that רב חסא said that רבי אמי asked: These items have no law of אונאה. Do they still have cancellation of the sale, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי אמי asks about items, like land, that are not covered by the laws of overcharging (אונאה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, an overcharge of one-sixth must be refunded, and more than a sixth can cancel the sale. For items with no אונאה, the small overcharge is certainly ignored. The question is whether a huge price gap can still cancel the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: he asked, he raised a question
the law about overcharging or underpaying
cancelling the sale

phrases.english: רבא said: רב חסא said,
רבי אמי asks:
They have no law of overcharging;
phrases.notes: "They" means the items the משנה excluded from אונאה, such as land and הקדש.

phrases.english: do they have cancellation of the sale
or do they not have it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the previous question ended in תיקו
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does being excluded from אונאה also exclude an item from ביטול מקח?

steps.title: רבי אמי answers his own question: the sale can be cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן reports that רבי אמי later decided: these items have no אונאה, but they do have ביטול מקח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said that רב חסא later said that רבי אמי resolved it: They have no אונאה, but they do have cancellation of the sale.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי now answers the question he asked in step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being excluded from אונאה only removes the rule about a one-sixth overcharge. When the price is very far off, the sale can still be cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: he later said, he came back and said
he resolved, he answered the question

steps.whatToRemember: Items excluded from אונאה are not fully protected deals. A big enough price error can still cancel the sale.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הֲדַר אָמַר רַב חַסָּא,
phrases.english: רב נחמן said: רב חסא later said,
רבי אמי resolved it:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹנָאָה אֵין לָהֶם, בִּיטּוּל מִקָּח יֵשׁ לָהֶם.
phrases.english: They have no overcharging law, but they do have cancellation of the sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר רַב חַסָּא, פָּשֵׁיט רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No אונאה, but yes ביטול מקח.

steps.title: Two students quote רבי יוחנן, each about a different item
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונה applies the ruling to הקדש, and רבי ירמיה applies it to land. Both quote רבי יוחנן: no אונאה, but yes ביטול מקח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונה said it about consecrated property. רבי ירמיה said it about land. Both said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They have no אונאה, but they do have cancellation of the sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ruling is now quoted from רבי יוחנן, but the two people quoting him disagree about which items it was said about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree on the wording of the ruling. They disagree only about its subject: הקדשות or קרקעות. The next step explains what each version means for the other item.

keyTerms.meaning: property consecrated to the בית המקדש
land, real estate
both of them
in the name of

phrases.english: רבי יונה said it about consecrated property;
רבי ירמיה said it about land;
and both of them said in the name of רבי יוחנן:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹנָאָה אֵין לָהֶם, בִּיטּוּל מִקָּח יֵשׁ לָהֶן.
phrases.english: They have no overcharging law, but they do have cancellation of the sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹנָה אָמַר אַהֶקְדֵּשׁוֹת, רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר אַקַּרְקָעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel version of the same ruling from רבי יוחנן and narrows down which items it covers
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per רבי יוחנן, the items have no אונאה but do have ביטול מקח. רבי יונה says this was said about הקדש, and רבי ירמיה says it was said about land.

steps.title: How the two versions relate, using שמואל's ruling
steps.stepSummary: If the ruling was said about הקדש, it applies to land all the more. If it was said about land, it does not apply to הקדש, as שמואל holds that הקדש redeemed for any amount is redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who said it about consecrated property would hold it all the more about land. The one who said it about land would not hold it about consecrated property, in line with שמואל. שמואל said: Consecrated property worth a מנה that someone redeemed onto something worth a פרוטה is redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what each version means for the other item: does the rule carry over from one to the other?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הקדש version covers land too, as a קל וחומר. The land version holds that הקדש is different: following שמואל, redeeming הקדש works even for a tiny price, so a price gap can never cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: all the more so
a large sum, one hundred דינרים
the smallest coin of value
redeemed; its holiness has moved off it

steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל's rule shows that for הקדש, a lopsided price does not undo the redemption at all. That is why הקדש might be different from land.

phrases.english: The one who said it about consecrated property,
all the more so about land.
The one who said it about land,
but not about consecrated property,
in line with שמואל, for שמואל said:
Consecrated property worth a מנה
that one redeemed onto something worth a פרוטה is redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר אַהֶקְדֵּשׁוֹת, כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן אַקַּרְקָעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the practical gap between the two versions in step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under the הקדש version, both land and הקדש have ביטול מקח. Under the land version, only land has it, because of שמואל's rule that הקדש redeemed for even a פרוטה is redeemed.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree that land has ביטול מקח. They argue only about הקדש.

steps.title: A משנה about a blemished sacred animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a blemished sacred animal becomes non-sacred, and its value must be made up.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: If the sacred animal was blemished, it becomes non-sacred, and one must make up its value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from another מסכת. It is setting up the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives two results. The blemished animal leaves its holy status, and the price difference must still be paid to הקדש. The next step asks where each of these two results comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: we learned in a משנה elsewhere
blemished
it becomes non-sacred
to make up its value in money

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: "There" is a משנה in מסכת תמורה.

phrases.english: If the sacred animal was blemished,
it becomes non-sacred,
and one must make up its value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source about the value of הקדש, a topic close to the discussion of הקדש and price gaps in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blemished sacred animal becomes non-sacred, but its value must be made up.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: making up the value is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the animal becomes non-sacred by Torah law, but the duty to make up its value is rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It becomes non-sacred by Torah law, and the duty to make up its value is from the words of the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן splits the משנה's two results into two different levels of law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, the redemption works fully even without the full value. Paying the difference was added by the רבנן. This fits well with שמואל's idea that הקדש redeemed for a small amount is still redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: by Torah law
from the words of the רבנן; rabbinic

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
It becomes non-sacred: by Torah law;
and one must make up its value: by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: יָצָא לְחוּלִּין – דְּבַר תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source level of each part of the משנה in step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Becoming non-sacred is a Torah law. Making up the value is rabbinic.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: making up the value is a Torah law too
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says that even the duty to make up the value comes from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Even the duty to make up its value is from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש disagrees with רבי יוחנן about the second part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that the animal becomes non-sacred. For ריש לקיש, the Torah itself also requires paying הקדש the missing value. This sets up the questions the גמרא will ask next.

keyTerms.meaning: even, also
from the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says paying the missing value to הקדש is rabbinic, and ריש לקיש says it is a Torah law. Both agree the animal becomes non-sacred.

phrases.english: And ריש לקיש said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף צָרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ דָּמִים מִן הַתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: Even the duty to make up its value is from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אַף צָרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ דָּמִים מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יוחנן in step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making up the value of the blemished sacred animal is a Torah requirement.

steps.title: If the shortfall is exactly a sixth, ריש לקיש is hard to explain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which case is being discussed. If the animal was redeemed for a sixth less than its value (אונאה), why would ריש לקיש require Torah-level payment, when a משנה says הקדש has no אונאה?
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we talking about? Say the difference is exactly the amount of overcharging (a sixth). Would ריש לקיש really say the person must make up the value by Torah law? But a משנה teaches: these things have no overcharging rule: land, slaves, documents, and consecrated property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts checking how big the gap was between the animal's real value and the price paid. It tries the first option, a gap of exactly a sixth, and shows that this does not fit ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gap of exactly a sixth is the normal overcharging (אונאה) case. The משנה says הקדש is not covered by אונאה at all. So in that case there should be no Torah duty to pay the difference, and ריש לקיש's view that the duty is from the Torah does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
The amount of overcharging, exactly one sixth
To make up its value (pay the difference to הקדש)
Consecrated property

phrases.english: With what case are we dealing?
If we say it is by the amount of overcharging,
phrases.notes: He means the animal was redeemed for exactly a sixth less than it was worth.

phrases.english: would ריש לקיש say in this case:

phrases.aramaic: צָרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ דָּמִים דְּבַר תּוֹרָה?
phrases.english: he must make up its value by Torah law?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
These are things that have no overcharging rule:
land, and slaves,
and documents, and consecrated property!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש by asking what size of shortfall they mean.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view (Step 9) that making up the value is from the Torah
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the gap is only a sixth, the משנה says הקדש has no אונאה, so no Torah duty to pay should exist.

steps.title: If the shortfall cancels the sale, רבי יוחנן is hard to explain
steps.stepSummary: Try the other option: the gap was more than a sixth (ביטול מקח). Then how can רבי יוחנן call the duty only rabbinic, when he himself is quoted saying that הקדש and land do have ביטול מקח?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the gap is big enough to cancel the sale. Would רבי יוחנן say in this case that he must make up the value only by rabbinic law? But רבי יונה said about consecrated property, and רבי ירמיה said about land, and both said in the name of רבי יוחנן: they have no overcharging rule, but they do have canceling of the sale!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second option, a gap of more than a sixth, and shows that this does not fit רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5 רבי יוחנן was quoted saying that הקדש does have ביטול מקח. So when the gap is more than a sixth, there should be a real Torah issue with the redemption. That clashes with his view in Step 8 that the duty to pay is only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancelling the sale, when the price is off by more than a sixth
By rabbinic law
But didn't (so-and-so) say?
Both of them

phrases.english: Rather, it is the amount that cancels the sale,
phrases.notes: Meaning the gap was more than a sixth.

phrases.english: would רבי יוחנן say in this case
that he must make up its value only by rabbinic law?
But didn't רבי יונה say about consecrated property,
and רבי ירמיה said about land,
and both of them said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
they have no overcharging rule,
but they do have canceling of the sale!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בִּיטּוּל מִקָּח, בְּהָא לֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the first option failed for ריש לקיש, the גמרא tries the second option, and it fails for רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view (Step 8) that making up the value is only rabbinic
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן himself said הקדש has ביטול מקח, so a gap of more than a sixth should matter by Torah law.

steps.title: The case is cancelling the sale, and the names are switched
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case really is ביטול מקח. The opinions must be switched: רבי יוחנן says the duty is from the Torah, and ריש לקיש says it is rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really it is the case of canceling the sale. Switch the opinions: what we said in the name of רבי יוחנן belongs to ריש לקיש, and what we said in the name of ריש לקיש belongs to רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by keeping the ביטול מקח case and swapping who said what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the swap, רבי יוחנן says the payment is a Torah duty. That fits his own statement that הקדש has ביטול מקח. ריש לקיש now says the payment is only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (keeping the earlier option)
Switch, reverse (the names of the opinions)

steps.whatToRemember: After the switch, רבי יוחנן says making up the value is from the Torah, and ריש לקיש says it is rabbinic. The case is a gap of more than a sixth.
steps.confusionAlert: For the explanations about שמואל in steps 13 to 15, read steps 8 and 9 with the names swapped. Otherwise they will seem backwards. Step 16 then offers a different answer that keeps the original names.

phrases.english: Really, it is the case of canceling the sale,
and switch: the view of רבי יוחנן goes to ריש לקיש,
and the view of ריש לקיש goes to רבי יוחנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem from Step 11 by swapping the names.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching the attributions of the opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוחנן said the duty was rabbinic, which clashed with his own ruling about ביטול מקח.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן says it is from the Torah, and ריש לקיש says it is rabbinic, in a case of more than a sixth.

steps.title: What is their argument based on?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the opinions are set, the גמרא asks what idea lies behind the argument.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to explain the reasoning behind the two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The facts of the case are now clear. The question is what principle makes one say Torah and the other say rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they argue?

phrases.english: About what do they argue?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the switched opinions and asks for their root.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle behind the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש

steps.title: They argue about whether שמואל's rule is correct
steps.stepSummary: The argument depends on שמואל, who said that הקדש worth a מנה redeemed for a פרוטה is redeemed. One master holds like שמואל and one does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about שמואל's rule, for שמואל said: consecrated property worth a hundred that one redeemed onto something worth a פרוטה is redeemed. One master holds like שמואל, and one master does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the whole argument depends on whether you accept שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If redeeming for a פרוטה fully works by Torah law (שמואל), then paying the rest can only be a rabbinic rule. That is ריש לקיש. רבי יוחנן does not accept שמואל, so the full value is owed by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: He redeemed it, moving the holiness onto something else
It is redeemed (no longer holy)
A large sum, one hundred דינרים
One master holds of (this view)

phrases.english: About the rule of שמואל,
for שמואל said:
Consecrated property worth a hundred
that one redeemed onto something worth a פרוטה is redeemed.
One master holds like שמואל,
phrases.notes: This is ריש לקיש, so for him the extra payment is only rabbinic.

phrases.english: and one master does not hold like שמואל.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ריש לקיש accepts שמואל, so the payment is rabbinic. רבי יוחנן rejects שמואל, so the payment is from the Torah.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties this argument to שמואל's rule, which was already mentioned in Step 6.

steps.title: Second version: both accept שמואל, but argue about doing it from the start
steps.stepSummary: Another way to explain it: both accept שמואל. One holds his rule works only after the fact, and the other holds it applies even from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: everyone holds like שמואל, and here they argue about this. One master holds: if he already redeemed it, yes, it works, but he may not do it from the start. The other master holds: it is allowed even from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second explanation of the argument, in which both sides accept שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says שמואל's rule works only after the fact. Since one may not redeem cheaply from the start, the Torah still requires the full value. ריש לקיש says it is fine even from the start, so the extra payment is only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (a second explanation)
Everyone
From the start, as the proper way to act

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain the argument. Either they argue about whether שמואל is right, or both accept שמואל and argue about whether one may redeem cheaply from the start.

phrases.english: If you want, say:
everyone holds like שמואל,
and here they argue about this:
one master holds: if he already redeemed it, yes, it works,
but from the start, no.
And one master holds: even from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question in Step 13, different from Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both accept שמואל. רבי יוחנן says it works only after the fact, so the payment is from the Torah. ריש לקיש says it is allowed even from the start, so the payment is rabbinic.

steps.title: Another answer: keep the case as a one-sixth gap and keep the opinions as they were
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the first option: the gap was exactly a sixth. It does not switch the opinions. It says the argument depends on רב חסדא's idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say this instead: really the gap was exactly the amount of אונאה, and do not switch the opinions. They argue about the idea of רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new way to answer the earlier problem. It keeps the case as a one-sixth gap and leaves the names where they started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא switched the opinions because it understood the case as ביטול מקח. Now it says the case can be a gap of exactly one sixth with no switch. The two אמוראים simply disagree about רב חסדא's explanation, which comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: introduces another possible answer
Really, actually: going back to an earlier option
The amount of overcharging that counts as אונאה, one sixth
Do not switch the opinions
They argue about

steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel step 15 or the earlier answers. It is just another possible way to explain the same argument.

phrases.english: If you want, say: really, it was the amount of overcharging,
and do not switch the opinions,
and they argue about the idea of רב חסדא,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם בִּכְדֵי אוֹנָאָה, וְלָא תֵּיפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another answer to the challenge in step 10, instead of the switch in step 12. It keeps the one-sixth case and the original names, and explains the argument through רב חסדא's idea.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what the argument depends on, so the opinions do not need to be switched
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A one-sixth gap could not work, so the opinions had to be switched and the case had to be ביטול מקח
steps.terutzMaskana: The case can be a one-sixth gap with the original opinions, if the argument is about רב חסדא's idea

steps.title: רב חסדא explains what 'they have no אונאה' means
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains the משנה's words 'אין להם אונאה' this way: these items are not under the system of אונאה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: what does 'they have no אונאה' mean? It means they are not under the rules of אונאה at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב חסדא's explanation, which the argument depends on. His sentence keeps going in the next part, so this step is setting up what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might read 'אין להם אונאה' as a leniency, meaning there is never a refund. רב חסדא says it means these items stand outside the normal one-sixth system. The next words will explain what rule applies to them instead.

keyTerms.meaning: They have no law of overcharging: the משנה's words about הקדש and similar items
Under the system or rules of אונאה

steps.whyThisMatters: The disagreement between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש will turn on whether they accept this reading of the משנה.

phrases.english: who said: what does 'they have no overcharging' mean?
they are not under the rules of overcharging at all,
phrases.notes: His sentence isn't finished. The next amud tells us what rule applies to them instead.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר: מַאי אֵין לָהֶם אוֹנָאָה? אֵינָן בְּתוֹרַת אוֹנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the רב חסדא statement that step 16 said the argument depends on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'אין להם אונאה' means these items are outside the system of אונאה altogether. It does not simply mean there is no refund. The full rule continues on the next amud.
